Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution 

$$
X_1(s) = \mathcal{L}\left\{ x_1(t) \right\} = \dfrac{4}{s} + \dfrac{1}{s-6}, 
\qquad
X_2(s) = \mathcal{L}\left\{ x_2(t) \right\} = \dfrac{20}{s} - \dfrac{1}{s-6}.
$$

Find the solution to the original initial value problem.
question.worked_solution:
To find $x_1(t)$ and $x_2(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to $X_1(s)$ and $X_2(s){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{1}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{4}{s}+\frac{1}{s-6}\} \\  & =4{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\}+{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-6}\} \\  & =4\cdot 1+{e}^{6\cdot t} \\  & =4+{e}^{6t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{2}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{20}{s}-\frac{1}{s-6}\} \\  & =20{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\}-{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-6}\} \\  & =20\cdot 1-{e}^{6\cdot t} \\  & =20-{e}^{6t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4+{e}^{6t} \\ 20-{e}^{6t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 20\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{6t}\end{aligned}
$$
